headline: Earnings rise on record fee income and lower charge-offs
summary_short: Regions' Q3 2026 net income was $631M and diluted EPS $0.71 (+16% y/y, adjusted $0.73); net interest margin rose to 3.68% and charge-offs fell to 0.29%.
summary_long: Net interest income grew 1.6% q/q to $1.30B. Capital markets income rose 27% q/q to $107M and the quarter set records in capital markets (excluding valuation adjustments) and treasury management. Average loans rose 0.5% on C&I growth. Annualized net charge-offs fell to 0.29% from 0.42%, and the allowance ratio was 1.61%. Reported return on average tangible common equity was 21.3%. Estimated CET1 was 10.8%, and interest-bearing deposit costs were 1.70%.
confidence_notes: Y/y EPS growth is as stated in the release. Net income, adjusted EPS and efficiency q/q changes are computed from the two-quarter table. CET1 is the company's estimate. Detailed reconciliations are in a separate Exhibit 99.2 that was not read.

drivers.explanation: Strong credit quality, continued momentum in fee-based businesses and economically vibrant markets, per the CEO; charge-offs also fell sequentially.
A hedging program that leaves a mostly neutral short-term rate position supported the margin, alongside low-cost deposits.
Management cited investments in talent, technology and strategic growth, with expenses held in check.
